## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sitthāvakāraka Sikkhāpada* (“Scattering rice,” Sekhiya 48) is a training rule for Buddhist monastics located in the Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga of the Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The rule belongs to the *sekhiya* section of the monastic code, which sets out standards of proper deportment and table manners, specifically instructing monastics not to drop or scatter particles of rice while eating [SuttaCentral]. A modern English translation has been prepared by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].

Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral show that this regulation is shared widely across early Buddhist monastic traditions [SuttaCentral]. In the Pali Vinaya, exact counterparts exist in the Bhikkhu Pātimokkha (Sk 48), the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga and Pātimokkha (Sk 48), and the Bhikkhu and Bhikkhunī Parivāra (Sk 48) [SuttaCentral]. Parallels in other Vinaya lineages are preserved in Chinese and Sanskrit across multiple early schools, including the Sarvāstivāda (e.g., Chinese Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Sk 77; Sanskrit Prātimokṣa Sk 80, Sk 81), Mūlasarvāstivāda (Chinese Sk 58; Sanskrit Sk 58, Sk 59), Mahīśāsaka (Chinese Sk 59), Dharmaguptaka (Chinese Sk 40), Mahāsāṅghika (Chinese Sk 40; Sanskrit Sk 42), and Lokottaravāda (Sanskrit Bhikkhu Prātimokṣa Sk 42, Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Sk 43) [SuttaCentral].

No cross-language alignments reach the match threshold in DharmaNexus [DharmaNexus].
